column3: This is VLA Forge. You describe a task in plain words, and it trains a robot policy for it. Building a skill from one sentence needs a frontier model, and here that model is Llama. All of this runs in simulation.
The canvas starts blank. I type one task for an SO-101: push the blue block onto the white square.
Every step is a message between Fetch.ai uAgents. Fetch.ai is the multi-agent orchestration, and Llama powers the reasoning agents: task, critic and optimizer.
Back on the canvas, the robot flies to the stage being worked on and points at it with its gripper.
The agents collect demos, fine-tune from the closest skill, then test the policy on {n} scenes it never saw. The waiting is sped up four times, and the badge shows it.
Press T and the Thinking panel shows each agent's reasoning as it happens. I ask what it is doing, and it answers from the live run.
The first round got {r1} of {rn}, under the bar, so the critic sent it back for another.
The new skill trained in {t} seconds and got {s} of {n} held-out scenes, in simulation.
Now I type add another SO-101, and a second arm appears in place.
Then I describe a task for two arms: one seats the housing in the pallet, and the other inserts it into the socket.
The Arms list gives plain results: {ac} of {an} tries finished by both arms, in simulation.

Next, the Optimize step. Llama plans the task, critiques the failures, and now optimizes. This is a saved run on socket insertion, and each round it reads where the skill fails and proposes one change.
Each tile is one selection scene, blue for a success and red for a failure. A change is kept only if success rises on these same one hundred scenes.
Round zero got {o0} of one hundred. Rounds one, three and five were kept, and rounds two and four were reverted. The last kept round, round five, got {ob}.

Selection scores can flatter a policy, so here are one hundred test scenes the optimizer never saw. Round zero got {h0} of one hundred, and the final policy got {hf}. Random changes over the same rounds went from {c0} to {cf}. That is plus seven, not yet significant, with p of point three four. All of it in simulation.
That is VLA Forge: describe a task, add arms, and let Llama optimize the skill, measured in simulation.
